newsitem.title: UK: Lufthansa to warn of future fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to warn of future fuel surcharge.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG's UK unit will in future attempt to give shippers and agents 30 days' notice of any fuel surcharges imposed, its UK and Ireland director Bob Bingley said.
He told Reuters that he expected the carrier would adopt this policy on a worldwide basis and that other airlines would also soon follow suit.
This action follows immediate surcharges introduced last November on top of cargo rates by Lufthansa and many other carriers to counter spiralling jet fuel costs.

"Nobody involved in the air cargo industry disputed the need for these surcharges but shippers complained that we the airlines gave no notice whatsoever of their introduction. Shippers were left with passing the information on to their customes and we understand the difficulties they were confronted with," he said.

"We will now closely monitor fuel prices as they go up and down. If there is a disaster, like a war suddenly breaking out in the Middle East, then fuel surcharges may have to be immediately imposed. But wherever possible in future, we will grant shippers 30 days' notice procedure," Bingley aded.

Andrew Traill, shipping and air manager of the Freight Transport Association, which represents shippers through its British Shippers' Council division, said he was "extremely pleased" to learn of Lufthansa's initiative.

"I understand that other airlines have also agreed on the 30 days' notice philosophy relating to fuel surcharges and this news represents a major step forward both for shippers and for the improvement of relations in this industry," he said.
He agreed that shippers had no basic complaints about the last round of fuel surcharges but were annoyed about their sudden imposition without warning.

"The decision to give shippers a 30-day early warning system represents yet another move towards the creation of a new age in relationships between shippers, freight forwarders and airlines," added Traill.
